paper_title: SepLLM Accelerate Large Language Models by Compressing One Segment into   One Separator
caption_used: Training loss curves over iterations for Vanilla, StrmLLM (n=64), and four SepLLM configurations. All models start with loss values exceeding 3.4 and converge as training progresses to 140,000 iterations. The Vanilla model achieves the lowest final loss at approximately 2.45, while StrmLLM (n=64) converges to roughly 2.60, showing a notable gap from the SepLLM variants. Among the SepLLM configurations, the H/T variant reaches the lowest loss at approximately 2.49, with SepLLM (n=128) settling at approximately 2.55, slightly above both the base SepLLM (n=64) and SepLLM (n=64, H) which converge near 2.51-2.52. The most rapid decrease in loss occurs within the first 20,000 iterations for all models, after which convergence slows considerably.
model_annotation: The plot displays training loss curves over iterations for six different model configurations: Vanilla, StrmLLM (n=64), and four variants of SepLLM (n=64), (n=64, H), (n=64, H/T), and (n=128). The x-axis represents the number of iterations, ranging from 0 to 140,000 on a linear scale, with tick marks at intervals of 20,000. The y-axis shows the loss value, ranging from 2.4 to 3.4 on a linear scale, with tick marks at intervals of 0.1. All models begin with a loss exceeding 3.4 at iteration 0 and exhibit a rapid decline in loss during the first 20,000 iterations. After this initial phase, the rate of loss reduction slows significantly, with all curves approaching convergence by 140,000 iterations. The Vanilla model (purple line with no markers, solid) achieves the lowest final loss, stabilizing at approximately 2.45. The StrmLLM (n=64) model (blue line with no markers, solid) converges to a loss of approximately 2.60. Among the SepLLM variants, the SepLLM (n=64, H/T) configuration (red line with no markers, solid) reaches the lowest loss at approximately 2.49, followed by SepLLM (n=128) (dark blue line with no markers, solid) at approximately 2.55. The base SepLLM (n=64) (orange line with no markers, solid) and SepLLM (n=64, H) (green line with no markers, solid) both converge to losses near 2.51–2.52. All curves show minor fluctuations, likely due to stochastic training dynamics, but maintain a generally smooth downward trend throughout the training process.
